subject: Private deployment DPA — access floorplan & customer key playbook
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@acmehealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procure@acmehealth.com
Date: 2025-06-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on DPA for on‑prem deployment and key custody

Hi Vanessa,

Following our discovery call, legal and security asked us to confirm a few items before procurement will move forward with the private deployment order:

- We need explicit DPA language that confirms operator access limitations for on‑prem / VPC deployments (no model input egress to Redwood unless customer consents).
- Clarify custody model for customer‑managed keys: can keys stay entirely in our KMS? If not, what escrow options exist?
- Subprocessor list for any partner that would have access to telemetry or logs.
- Cross‑border transfer policy for logs/telemetry — Acme cannot permit export outside US without prior approval.

Attached: customer_privacy_questionnaire.pdf (high level checklist from our InfoSec).

Can you point us to a redlined DPA and a short diagram showing the operator access floorplan? Procurement timeline target: finalize legal by 7/2.

Thanks,
Sarah Park
Director of Security, Acme Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: procure@acmehealth.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA for on‑prem deployment and key custody

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses below and I attached a short playbook and a floorplan for the architecture: CustKey_Playbook_v1.docx, network-access-floorplan.png.

High‑level answers:
- Operator access: For private VPC/on‑prem, Redwood operators do not get default access to plaintext customer payloads. We enforce role‑based access (support, infra, breakglass) and all operator actions are logged and reviewed.
- Keys: We support customer‑managed keys in the customer KMS (BYOK). For customers who require escrow, we offer an HSM escrow workflow (optional) — we can include escrow language in the DPA addendum.
- Subprocessors: Current subprocessors that may touch telemetry are: CloudOpsPartner Inc. (managed infra), MetricsLint (observability). We'll provide a full subprocessor registry and POA in the redline.
- Cross‑border: We can commit to US‑only processing and telemetry retention for Acme (geofenced regions) and exclude any telemetry export outside the US without explicit approval.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will share a redline of the DPA with suggested operator‑access and KMS escrow clauses.
2) Kimberly (security) will add a minimal operator access policy snippet.
3) Schedule a 30min call with Acme legal + security for 6/19 or 6/20 to confirm wording.

Attachments: CustKey_Playbook_v1.docx (playbook), network-access-floorplan.png (ops floorplan)

If that looks good I’ll prepare the redline and loop in Aditya for the legal addendum.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@acmehealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procure@acmehealth.com, secops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2025-06-18T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA for on‑prem deployment and key custody

Thanks Vanessa,

A few follow ups from SecOps & Procurement:
- Escrow: we need sample escrow language and the technical flow (who can request key retrieval, what triggers it, audit trail).
- Telemetry: confirm whether runtime traces include any redacted prompt tokens or only aggregate metrics. We expect full redaction of any PII in telemetry.
- Artifacts: can you provide a SOC 2 Type II summary and an example model dataflow diagram (we need to attach to our procurement packet).

Preferred meeting window: 6/19 10–12 PT.

Regards,
Sarah

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-18T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: internal — suggested redline / minimal operator access snippet

Vanessa / Aditya,

Looping in suggested language we should put in the DPA addendum for on‑prem/VPC customers who require strict custody:

1) Operator Access Limitation: "Redwood will not access, use, or copy Customer Content for any purpose other than performing the Services, and will limit operator access to metadata and health telemetry only. Any operator access to Customer Content will require documented approval from the Customer Data Owner and will be constrained to an auditable breakglass workflow."

2) KMS & Escrow: "Customer retains sole control of cryptographic keys. Redwood will only have access to key material if and when the Customer initiates a documented escrow request for recovery; such requests require dual‑control approval from the Customer's security contacts and are logged to the Customer's audit trail."

3) Subprocessors & Geo: include clause for geofencing: "Telemetry and logs related to Customer deployments will be stored and processed only within the US region specified in the SOW unless Customer provides prior written consent for transfer."

I recommend we attach the playbook and the floorplan. Aditya — can you prepare the DPA redline PDF (we should include a doc link back to HubSpot HS-98721).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@acmehealth.com>, secops@acmehealth.com, procure@acmehealth.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-19T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment DPA — consolidated plan and redline link

Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround. We consolidated internal feedback and prepared a redline. Summary of commitments below and attached: Redwood_DPA_v2_redlines.pdf.

Summary of proposed items for Acme:
- Operator access: explicit prohibition on routine human review of customer content for private VPC/on‑prem. Breakglass only, dual approval, full audit trail surfaced to customer.
- Keys: BYOK supported. Escrow process: customer‑initiated, documented, requires dual auth from Acme security contacts; Redwood will maintain immutable proof logs and will never unilaterally retrieve keys.
- Telemetry: runtime telemetry excludes raw prompt/response tokens and PII is redacted at capture. Retention limited to the window in SOW; geofenced to US only.
- Subprocessors: full registry appended to the redline; CloudOpsPartner and MetricsLint are named and covered by subprocessor agreements.
- Evidence: attached SOC2 summary and model dataflow diagram will be posted to the Drive link (see related_links).

Next steps:
1) Review redline PDF and the playbook.
2) Legal call 6/20 10:30 PT (I’ve penciled this — please confirm).
3) If the redline is acceptable, Procurement to issue PO and we’ll prepare the Private Deployment SOW (geo, retention windows, SLOs).

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2_redlines.pdf, CustKey_Playbook_v1.docx, network-access-floorplan.png
HubSpot deal: HS-98721

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v2_redlines.pdf (redlined DPA), CustKey_Playbook_v1.docx (operator playbook), network-access-floorplan.png (ops floorplan)
